MUQATIL:3:189-191/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:189-191/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:189-191/r2.claim: The creation of the heavens and earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for people of reason.

ZAJJAJ:v1p498/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p498/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p498/r2.claim: Ūlū al-albāb means people possessing intellect, and the signs are evidences of the Creator’s oneness.

IBNABIHATIM:v3p841#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p841#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p841#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Quraysh asked the Prophet to make Safa into gold; after he prayed, this verse was revealed.

SULAMI:v1p130/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p130/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p130/r1.claim: The verse lets ordinary believers infer the Creator from created things and their signs; people of spiritual realities are addressed instead with direct vision of the Lord.

SULAMI:v1p130/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p130/r2.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p130/r2.claim: Anyone who establishes God through a cause has established something other than Him, since a cause entails an effect and the Real is above that relation.

SULAMI:v1p130/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p130/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p130/r3.claim: Commoners affirm God through what befits Him, while the elect transcend every description the commoners apply; the former know through servanthood and the latter through lordship.

SULAMI:v1p130/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p130/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p130/r4.claim: The elect see the cosmos and events only as signs, and see those signs by witnessing the Real within them; such witnessing leaves no taste of createdness in the heart.

SULAMI:v1p130/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p130/r5.speaker: النصرآباذي
SULAMI:v1p130/r5.claim: Those without inner understanding find no lesson in contemplating heaven and earth; people of understanding view creation through the eye of the Real.

THALABI:v3p230/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p230/r1.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v3p230/r1.claim: Aisha recounts the Prophet’s tearful night prayer and his answer that he should be a grateful servant; he said the verse had been revealed that night and warned readers who fail to reflect.

THALABI:v3p230/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p230/r2.speaker: محمد بن علي عن أبيه
THALABI:v3p230/r2.claim: The Prophet would use the toothstick at night, look to the sky, and recite the passage through the plea to be protected from the Fire.

THALABI:v3p230/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p230/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن بريدة عن أبيه
THALABI:v3p230/r3.claim: The Prophet called this passage the most severe verse of the Qurʾan for the jinn.

THALABI:v3p230/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p230/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v3p230/r4.claim: After learning of Moses’ and Jesus’ signs, Quraysh asked the Prophet to turn al-Safa into gold; this verse was revealed instead.

QUSHAYRI:v1p188/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p188/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p188/r1.claim: Signs for ordinary people lie in outward horizons, while signs for the elect lie within themselves; the first yield knowledge of certainty and the second direct vision.

QUSHAYRI:v1p188/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p188/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p188/r2.claim: Changing night and day signifies different spiritual nights: those in union find them short, while those in separation find them long.

QUSHAYRI:v1p188/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p188/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p188/r3.claim: Poems about unnoticed months, brief days of joy, and seemingly endless nights illustrate how spiritual attachment changes the felt passage of time.

QUSHAYRI:v1p188/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p188/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p188/r4.claim: People of sound understanding have recovered from heedless intoxication; sound vision looks from the Real toward the Real.

QUSHAYRI:v1p188/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p188/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p188/r5.claim: Looking from created things toward God can reverse one’s blessing and turn thought into doubt.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p138/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p138/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p138/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Quraysh asked Jews and Christians about Moses’ and Jesus’ signs, then demanded a golden Ṣafā from Muhammad; God instead pointed to creation and night-day as signs for the discerning.

JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r1.claim: Lubb means intellect: either it is superior to other human faculties as the kernel is to the husk, or it is the root of knowledge and guide to good as the kernel is a thing's origin.

JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r12.claim: The heavens' creation includes their origination, colors, structure, elevation, support, and adornment with stars; earth's creation includes its spread, wonders, plants, and mountains.

JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r13.claim: Night and day are signs through darkness and light, their waxing and waning, and their successive alternation; these are proofs for people of intellect.

JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r2.claim: Arab polytheists asked Jews for Moses' signs and Christians for Jesus' signs, then asked Muhammad to make Mount Ṣafā gold; the verse about creation was revealed.

JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r3.speaker: عائشة
JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r3.claim: A report from ʿĀʾisha says the Prophet prayed at night and wept; when Bilāl asked whether God had not forgiven him, he answered that he should be a grateful servant and explained that this verse had come to him that night.

JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r4.speaker: النبي
JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r4.claim: The Prophet warns that woe awaits someone who recites the verse without reflecting on it.

JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r5.claim: One coherence reading connects the passage to the claim that God is poor and people are rich: the owner of the heavens and earth cannot be poor.

JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1424#2/r9.claim: The verse about creation follows the statement of God's sovereignty: creation is evidence of His ownership and of His attributes for anyone who reflects.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p151/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p151/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p151/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet recited these verses repeatedly during the night, praying six long rakats in three pairs and then three witr rakats.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p151/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p151/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p151/r3.claim: After night prayer the Prophet asked God for light in his sight, hearing, speech, and around and above and below him; Kuraib's report adds light in the heart and on both sides.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p152/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p152/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p152/r1.claim: The people of understanding are those with intellect; the source segment ends just as their description is introduced.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p480/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p480/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p480/r2.claim: The cosmic signs clearly evidence the Creator, His immense power, and His striking wisdom.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p480/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p480/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p480/r3.claim: People of understanding look with insight, reasoning, and reflection rather than gazing like heedless animals.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p480/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p480/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p480/r4.claim: A short admonition urges people to study the stars and wonders of the universe, reflecting on their maker's power and wisdom before death ends the chance.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p480/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p480/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p480/r5.claim: Ibn Umar reports asking Aisha about what most amazed her in the Prophet; she begins an account of his night worship, prayer, and weeping, continued in the next segment.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p481/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p481/r1.speaker: عائشة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p481/r1.claim: Aisha recounts that the Prophet sought her permission for night worship, prayed and wept, and told Bilal he wept because God had sent down the signs of creation; he warned against reciting without reflection.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p481/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p481/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p481/r2.claim: Another report warns against mouthing the verse between one's jaws without contemplating it; no named authority or grading is given.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p481/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p481/r3.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p481/r3.claim: Ali reports that when the Prophet rose at night, he used a toothstick, looked toward the sky, and recited this verse.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p481/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p481/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p481/r4.claim: A story says an Israelite's cloud of shade failed after thirty years of worship; his mother attributes it to once looking at the sky without reflecting.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p553#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p553#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p553#2/r6.claim: The heavens, earth, and creatures provide evidence for a Creator and for knowledge; an existing knower and willing agent cannot be lifeless.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p553#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p553#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p553#2/r7.claim: Night and day alternate and differ in length as well as in light and darkness; ayat means signs.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p553#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p553#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p553#2/r8.claim: The people of understanding are intellects shaped by religious obligation rather than mere experience.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p526/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p526/r1.speaker: ابن جبير عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p526/r1.claim: After Quraysh heard that Moses had a staff and shining hand and Jesus healed blindness and leprosy and raised the dead, they asked for the Safa hill to become gold; this verse followed.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p526/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p526/r2.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p526/r2.claim: The people of Mecca asked the Prophet for a sign, and this verse was revealed.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p526/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p526/r3.speaker: أبو الضحى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p526/r3.claim: After 2:163, Quraysh said God had equated their deities with one another and demanded a sign.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p526/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p526/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p526/r4.claim: The interpretation of this verse was given earlier with 2:164.

RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r1.claim: After extended legal discussion and answers to opponents, the passage redirects hearts from created things toward knowing God, using the signs of divine unity, divinity, majesty, and greatness.

RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r2.claim: Ibn Umar reports Aisha's account that the Prophet asked permission for night worship, prayed and wept, then said this verse had been revealed that night and asked whether he should not be a grateful servant.

RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r3.claim: A prophetic warning says woe to anyone who recites the verse without reflecting on it; another wording warns against merely chewing it between the jaws without contemplation.

RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r4.speaker: علي
RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r4.claim: Ali reports that when the Prophet rose at night, he used a toothstick, looked toward the sky, and recited the verse.

RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r5.claim: An Israelite youth's cloud of shade failed to appear during worship; his mother suggested he had once looked at the sky without reflecting, and he recalled doing so.

RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p108#2/r6.claim: The verse repeats three signs from 2:164, whereas that passage lists eight and ends with people who reason; this difference raises questions about repetition, omitted signs, and the phrase possessors of intellect.

RAZI-FULL:v9p109/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p109/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p109/r1.claim: The heart's inner eye cannot focus fully on two objects at once: beginners need many proofs, but once divine knowledge illuminates the heart, fewer proofs allow fuller absorption in God.

RAZI-FULL:v9p109/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p109/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p109/r2.claim: Moses' command to remove his sandals in 20:12 alludes to leaving behind the premises that lead reason to knowledge when entering the sacred valley of divine oneness.

RAZI-FULL:v9p109/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p109/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p109/r3.claim: The eight signs in 2:164 suit an initial seeker; repeating only three celestial signs here, and omitting five earthly ones, signals that the realized knower should reduce attention to proofs, while heavenly signs are more overwhelming and wondrous.

RAZI-FULL:v9p109/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p109/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p109/r4.claim: The wording shifts from people who reason to possessors of intellect because reason has an outward and an inner core: the first stage is intellect, and its completed state is the core.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r1.claim: The surah closes by commanding reflection on God's signs in creation; this makes faith rest on certainty and evidence rather than imitation, since the signs proceed from the living, sustaining, powerful, holy, self-sufficient God.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r2.claim: People of understanding are those who use their minds to contemplate proofs.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r3.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r3.claim: Aisha reports that after this verse was revealed, the Prophet prayed and wept; when Bilal asked why, he said he should be a grateful servant and warned that woe awaits one who recites without reflecting. No grading is stated here.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r4.claim: Scholars recommend wiping the face on waking and beginning night prayer by reciting these ten verses, following the Prophet, then praying what one can; reflection joined to action is the best work discussed here.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r5.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet read ten verses from the end of Al-Imran each night; al-Wa'ili transmits it through Sulayman ibn Musa, Muzahir ibn Aslam, and al-Maqburi, with no grading stated.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r6.speaker: عثمان
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-191/r6.claim: A report from Uthman says whoever recites the end of Al-Imran at night is credited with spending the whole night in prayer.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:189-191/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:189-191/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:189-191/r2.claim: The heavens, earth, and alternation of night and day are clear proofs of the Creator's existence, unity, knowledge, and power for minds purified of sensory and imaginative confusion.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:189-191/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:189-191/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:189-191/r3.claim: These three signs encompass kinds of change: change in a thing itself, in its parts through changing forms, and in external relations through changing celestial positions.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:189-191/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:189-191/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:189-191/r4.claim: A prophetic warning says woe to the person who recites the signs without reflecting on them.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r1.claim: Creation and alternation are clear proofs of an eternal, knowing, wise, powerful Maker for people whose reason is free of desire, like a kernel freed from husk.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r2.claim: A substance cannot be free of a newly arising accident; what cannot be free of the originated is itself originated, so it requires an eternal originator rather than an infinite regress.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r3.claim: The beauty and precision of creation demonstrate knowledge and wisdom; its continuance demonstrates power.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r4.claim: A prophetic report warns of woe for someone who recites this verse without reflecting on it.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r5.claim: An Israelite worshipper received a cloud's shade after thirty years, but a young worshipper did not; his mother suggested he had failed to contemplate the sky, and he agreed.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p197#3/r6.claim: The Israelite youth's mother says he received no shade except because he had once looked at the sky without reflecting.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p468/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p468/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p468/r1.claim: Creation of the heavens and earth and alternation of night and day are clear signs of the Creator and His astonishing wisdom, apparent to people of intellect who reason and reflect.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p468/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p468/r2.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p468/r2.claim: Ibn Jubayr transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that Quraysh asked the Prophet to make Ṣafā gold after Jews and Christians mentioned Moses' miracles; this verse was revealed.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p468/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p468/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p468/r3.claim: The verse follows the declaration that God owns heaven and earth and is powerful, adding that their creation displays clear proofs to rational observers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p475#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p475#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p475#2/r5.claim: The author cites Abū Hurayra's report that the Prophet recited the last ten verses of Āl ʿImrān every night and says it is recommended for someone waking to wipe the face and begin prayer by reciting them, joining reflection with action.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r10.claim: It identifies repetition in the repeated warnings and in five occurrences of ‘Our Lord,’ among other paired expressions.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r11.claim: It identifies restriction in ‘for people of understanding’ and several other phrases, and matching wordplay in ‘believed, so we believed.’

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r12.claim: It begins a matching-wordplay example with ‘believed, so we believed.’

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r8.claim: One proposed rhetorical reading takes ḥisāb as a metaphor for recompense, as in the expression ‘I did not know my account.’

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r9.claim: The passage identifies antithesis in explaining, people and concealing, heaven and earth, night and day, standing and sitting, and male and female.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p487/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p487/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p487/r1.claim: The rhetorical inventory continues with matching wordplay in ‘believe, so we believed’ and in ‘any worker among you.’

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p487/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p487/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p487/r2.claim: It identifies nonmatching wordplay between a caller and calling, an allusion in ‘You did not create this in vain,’ and ellipsis in several places.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p183#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p183#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p183#2/r1.claim: A report says Quraysh asked Jews and Christians about Moses’ and Jesus’ miracles, then asked Muhammad to make Safa gold, after which this verse was revealed; Ibn Kathir calls the account problematic because the verse is Medinan but the request was Meccan.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p183#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p183#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p183#2/r2.claim: The heavens are high and vast, the earth low and dense, and both contain observable signs including celestial bodies, waters, mountains, plants, animals, minerals, and varied benefits.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p183#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p183#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p183#2/r3.claim: Night and day alternate, exchange length, become equal, then take length from one another by the decree of the Mighty and Wise.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p183#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p183#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p183#2/r4.claim: People of sound, discerning intellect grasp realities, unlike those who pass signs without understanding; Ibn Kathir cites the heedless passersby in 12:105–106.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r1.speaker: أبو سليمان الداراني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r1.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Darani says that every sight on leaving home reveals either a blessing owed gratitude or a lesson.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r10.speaker: مغيث الأسود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r10.claim: Mughith al-Aswad urges daily grave visits and imagining the judgment, its two destinations, and the terrors of Hell; he wept until he collapsed.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r11.speaker: عبد الله بن المبارك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r11.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak tells of a monk beside a graveyard and rubbish heap, where human remains and discarded goods both serve as worldly lessons.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r12.claim: Ibn Umar would test his heart at a ruin by asking where its former people were, then recalling that all things perish except God’s face.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas says two measured prayer cycles with a reflective heart are better than a night’s worship with an inattentive heart.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r14.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r14.claim: Al-Hasan advises leaving part of one’s stomach empty to make room for reflection.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r15.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r15.speaker: بعض الحكماء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r15.claim: Some sages say looking at the world without learning from it dims the heart’s inner sight in proportion to heedlessness.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r2.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says an hour of reflection is better than a night spent in worship.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r3.speaker: الفضيل عن الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r3.claim: Al-Fudayl quotes al-Hasan comparing reflection to a mirror that shows one’s good and bad deeds.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r4.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r4.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna calls reflection a light that enters the heart.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r5.claim: An unattributed couplet says a reflective person finds a lesson in everything.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r6.speaker: عيسى
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r6.claim: Jesus praises the person whose speech is remembrance, silence is reflection, and gaze draws lessons.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r7.speaker: لقمان الحكيم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r7.claim: Luqman says long solitude inspires reflection, and sustained reflection is like knocking at Paradise’s door.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r8.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r8.claim: Wahb says prolonged reflection leads to understanding, understanding to knowledge, and knowledge to action.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r9.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p184/r9.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz says speech in remembrance is good, but reflection on God’s blessings is better worship.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p187#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p187#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p187#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet’s household hosted him overnight; after the evening prayer, the Prophet rested, rose, praised God, and recited the closing verses of Aal Imran.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p187#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p187#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p187#2/r2.claim: Another Ibn Abbas report says the Prophet looked at the night sky, recited this verse through the surah’s end, and prayed for light throughout his body and at resurrection.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p187#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p187#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p187#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that Muslim, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa'i also transmit a related report through Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p188/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p188/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p188/r1.claim: The report about Quraysh asking for a golden Safa implies a Meccan setting, though the well-known classification of these verses is Medinan.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p188/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p188/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p188/r2.claim: Aisha recounts that the Prophet wept through prayer after this verse was revealed and told Bilal that one who reads it without reflection faces woe.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p188/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p188/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p188/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir treats Aisha’s report as evidence supporting the better-known Medinan dating of the verses.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p189/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p189/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p189/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir cites versions of the Aisha account through Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Hibban, and Ibn Abi al-Dunya.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p189/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p189/r2.speaker: سفيان الثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p189/r2.claim: A raised report attributed to Sufyan warns woe for one who reads the end of Aal Imran without reflecting, counting ten verses on his fingers.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p189/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p189/r3.speaker: الأوزاعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p189/r3.claim: Al-Awza'i says the minimum reflection that avoids this warning is to read the verses while understanding them.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p189/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p189/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p189/r4.claim: A report says the Prophet recited ten verses from the end of Aal Imran every night; Ibn Kathir identifies its transmitter مظاهر بن أسلم as weak.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p196/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p196/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p196/r4.claim: The vast, beneficial heavens and earth and the orderly alternation of night and day point to a changer and to the messengers' teachings, since their ordered course requires the decree of the Almighty, All-Knowing.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p196/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p196/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p196/r5.claim: Compared with the corresponding verse in al-Baqara, which presents eight kinds of proof, this passage offers three: beginners need many proofs, while the spiritually illuminated can be distracted by excess.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p196/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p196/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p196/r6.claim: This passage focuses on the heavens because their scale and wonders are more overpowering and lead the heart more quickly to God's grandeur; al-Baqara closes with reason, while this passage addresses those with insight beyond satanic whispers and illusion.

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p63/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p63/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p63/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Quraysh asked Jews about Moses's signs and Christians about Jesus's miracles, then asked Muhammad to turn Safa into gold; the verse directed them to reflect on signs in creation.

BURSEVI:v2p116#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p116#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p116#2/r1.claim: Meccans asked the Prophet for a sign proving his claim because he called them to worship God alone; the verse answered with signs in creation.

BURSEVI:v2p116#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p116#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p116#2/r2.claim: Signs lie in the great creation of heaven and earth, including sun, moon, stars, mountains, seas, trees, wild animals, and birds.

BURSEVI:v2p116#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p116#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p116#2/r3.claim: The alternation may mean night departing and day arriving, or their changing colors and lengths as each grows while the other shrinks with the sun's seasonal distance.

BURSEVI:v2p116#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p116#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p116#2/r4.claim: Lubb is the pure core of intellect: the mind first has ordinary reason and reaches its perfected inner core at the end of development.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p155#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155#2/r1.claim: Reports from the new astronomy that the sun is stationary at the world's center and other bodies move around it, with successful eclipse predictions, show that traditional astronomical models are not certain.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p155#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155#2/r2.claim: The variation of night and day may mean their waxing and waning as the sun's relative nearness and distance change over the seasons.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p155#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155#2/r3.claim: It may instead refer to local differences in day and night lengths and to different places simultaneously having night, day, morning, noon, or afternoon because Earth is spherical.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p155#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155#2/r4.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155#2/r4.claim: Ibn Arabi describes seven layered earths, each beneath a heavenly dome, with Earth spread flat beneath the sky and celestial bodies arranged across the heavens.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p155#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155#2/r5.claim: The author inclines to a spherical Earth while acknowledging Ibn Arabi's visionary account and disagreement between it and the majority of modern scholars and religious scholars.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p155/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155/r1.claim: The creation of heaven and earth confirms and proves the preceding statement; the verse opens with emphatic inna and no coordinating conjunction to signal its importance.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p155/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155/r2.claim: Night and day alternate as the sun rises and sets, itself swimming through the sea of God’s power according to divine will.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p155/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155/r3.claim: The claim that the heavens move while earth remains still conflicts with the majority Sunni view that the heavens are stationary and stars move by God’s decree; he identifies the former as the philosophers’ popular position.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p155/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155/r4.speaker: ابن عربي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p155/r4.claim: Ibn ʿArabī says the heavens are stationary spheres in which stars move measured courses, creating musical sounds through adjacent air; astronomers calculate motions and eclipses correctly but mistake their proposed physical ordering for reality.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r1.claim: No sound Prophetic reports give a fully detailed account of the heavens and Earth, since such detail is not among the Lawgiver's main concerns; what matters is clear.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r2.claim: Night is explained as a collective singular whose singular is layla, though other lexicographers regard it as a singular with no attested plural; the author rejects the plural-of-plurals analysis.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r3.claim: The delayed noun of إن is لآيات; its prefixed lām reflects its position after the predicate, and its indefinite form magnifies the signs, with a plural of paucity serving for abundance.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r4.claim: One interpretation sees the plural of paucity as hinting that visible signs, however numerous, are few beside the hidden signs in the treasuries of knowledge and unseen realms.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r5.claim: People of sound intellect are those whose minds are free of the impurities of sense and conjecture; the root لبّ has differing verb forms among Hijazis and Najdis.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r6.claim: A cited report uses لبّ for the finest camels, illustrating the word's sense of a pure or choice core.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r7.claim: Changes in the heavens and Earth entail origination and dependence on an eternal agent, establishing a maker and then divine oneness; their precise order also establishes perfect knowledge and power.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p156/r8.claim: Theologians use two arguments from these signs for a Creator: change and possibility; most prefer the argument from possibility.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p157#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p157#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v4p157#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says that while staying with his aunt Maymuna, he saw the Prophet wake around midnight, wipe sleep from his face, and recite the final ten verses of Al Imran.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p157/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p157/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p157/r1.claim: One explanation says these three signs represent heavenly, earthly, and composite phenomena; another ties them to change in an entity, its parts, and external configurations, but that latter account relies on philosophers' matter and form and is unsuitable as a basis for Qur'anic explanation.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p157/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p157/r2.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v4p157/r2.claim: The author favors the explanation that this passage stresses God's exclusive sovereignty and power, so it selects three major signs; al-Baqara adds signs of mercy because it also stresses God's wide mercy.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p157/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p157/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v4p157/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Quraysh asked Jews and Christians about Moses' and Jesus' signs, then asked Muhammad to turn al-Safa into gold; the verse was revealed in response.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p157/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p157/r4.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p157/r4.claim: Aisha recounts the Prophet praying through the night and weeping in standing, bowing, and prostration; he said he was a grateful servant and warned against reciting these verses without reflection.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p157/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p157/r5.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p157/r5.claim: A report from Ali says that when the Prophet rose at night he used a toothstick, looked toward the sky, and recited the verse.

ELMALILI:3:189-190/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r10.claim: The parallel in 2:164 gives eight kinds of proof for divine unity in fuller detail, while this verse condenses their basis and develops it toward spiritual progress.

ELMALILI:3:189-190/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r11.claim: The wording shifts from signs for people who reason in 2:164 to signs for people of inner intellect here: initial proof of unity needs reason, while progress in knowledge of God calls for a purified intellect.

ELMALILI:3:189-190/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r12.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r12.claim: Razi says a seeker first needs many proofs, but once the heart is lit by knowledge of God, fewer, summarized proofs help it avoid distraction and deepen contemplation; he connects this to Moses being told to remove his sandals (20:12).

ELMALILI:3:189-190/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r13.claim: In summary, the earlier passage seeks a journey toward God, whereas this passage seeks progress through God; the earlier follows the assertion of divine unity in 2:163, while this follows God's sovereignty in 3:189.

ELMALILI:3:189-190/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r14.claim: The present reflection concerns the manifestation and governance of God's kingdom and the purpose of creation; it is suited to mature minds and believing hearts refined by transmitted and rational knowledge and advanced in worship and knowledge.

ELMALILI:3:189-190/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r3.claim: Creation of the heavens and earth and the changing succession of night and day are countless signs of God's ownership, complete power, majesty, and greatness; they benefit people of sound, purified intellect.

ELMALILI:3:189-190/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r4.claim: The heavens and earth encompass all spatial beings, both higher and lower, implied by the concepts of space.

ELMALILI:3:189-190/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r5.claim: Creation means bringing beings into and removing them from existence in their essences, attributes, and modes of being, expressing real causation.

ELMALILI:3:189-190/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r6.claim: The succession and transformation of night and day convey time, relate to motion, and show that created beings are made and ordered.

ELMALILI:3:189-190/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r7.claim: The foundations of true knowledge are discovered by reflecting on the heavens and earth, night and day, creation and alternation, and the meaning of the inner intellect.

ELMALILI:3:189-190/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r8.speaker: Ubeyd b. Umeyr
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r8.claim: Ubeyd b. Umeyr recounts that Aisha described the Prophet's extraordinary night worship: he sought permission to pray, wept during prayer, and said he should be a grateful servant despite forgiveness.

ELMALILI:3:189-190/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:189-190/r9.claim: In the report from Aisha, the Prophet warns that woe awaits whoever recites this revelation without reflecting on it; another wording likens recitation without reflection to chewing it in the jaws.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p195#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p195#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p195#3/r1.claim: The discourse turns from the surah's preceding topics to reflection on creation and its signs, honoring those who heed them; this broad shift signals the surah's ending, which appropriately closes with admonition.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p195#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p195#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p195#3/r2.claim: إن emphasizes the importance of the report; creation may mean the ordered effects of making the heavens and earth or created things themselves, as in 31:11, while ulu al-albāb are people of perfected intellect.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p195#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p195#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p195#3/r3.claim: The signs in creation and alternating night and day were discussed at 2:164; remembering God can mean verbal remembrance or inward reflection.

TABATABAI:3:190-194/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:190-194/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:190-194/r2.claim: Creation here likely means the manner of existence and the created world's actions and changes, such as motion, rest, and transformation; these are among the chief observable signs.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r1.claim: This and following verses signal the surah's conclusion and summarize it through signs in creation and the believers' prayerful response.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r2.claim: Exegetes treat Al Imran as continuing Al-Baqara; its summary revisits monotheism, prophethood, the afterlife, and calls to Jews and Christians, preserving the surah's thematic unity with its opening.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r3.claim: Reason is a great gift but insufficient by itself for guidance; just as sight needs sunlight, reason needs revelation to grasp truth, especially the unseen.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r4.speaker: Râgıb el-İsfahânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r4.claim: Raghib calls reason God's inner messenger and the prophet the outer messenger: reason validates prophetic teaching, while religion without reason cannot live and reason without religion is confused; he connects them as light upon light.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r5.claim: Verses 190 onward show reason and revelation working together: observing the universe reveals its order and creator, leading people to deeper faith and prayer.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r6.claim: Verse 190 calls people to contemplate the creation of the heavens, earth, and their contents; this can lead to belief in an afterlife, accountability, avoidance of sin, and prayer for protection from punishment.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r7.claim: The Qur'an's written signs are paired with the universe as a book for reflection; this passage summarizes the chief cosmic proofs previously listed in greater scope in Al-Baqara 2:164.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r8.claim: Heavens, earth, celestial motion, and changing night and day are divine signs; rational reflection recognizes their infinite creator, understands the cosmos is not purposeless, and responds with humble worship.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:190/r9.claim: The next verse depicts remembering God in every posture and fearing the consequences of disobeying the creator and owner of the heavens and earth.

STUDYQURAN:3:190/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:190/r1.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:3:190/r1.claim: It is said that the Prophet recited verses 190–200 of this sūrah every night.

STUDYQURAN:3:190/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:190/r2.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:3:190/r2.claim: A report says Bilāl found the praying Prophet weeping when these verses were first revealed; asked why despite forgiveness, he answered that he should be a grateful servant and warned against reciting without reflection.

STUDYQURAN:3:190/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:190/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:190/r3.claim: Muslims are advised to read the verse and meditate deeply on its meanings, including their levels.

STUDYQURAN:3:190/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:190/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:190/r4.claim: Khalq can mean God's creative act or the created nature and qualities of the heavens and earth.

STUDYQURAN:3:190/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:190/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:190/r5.claim: The variation of night and day is also discussed in 2:164, 10:6, 23:80, and 45:5; 2:164 also mentions creation of the heavens and earth.

STUDYQURAN:3:190/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:190/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:190/r6.claim: The discussion of possessors of intellect (ūlu’l-albāb) is linked to 2:179, 39:9, 13:19, 14:52, 38:29, and 39:18.
